newsitem.title: CANADA: Hudson's Bay shares enjoy catch-up gains.
newsitem.headline: Hudson's Bay shares enjoy catch-up gains.

text.p: Shares in Hudson's Bay Co, Canada's largest department store chain operator, jumped in moderate trading on Thursday in a catch-up with movements in the rest of the merchandise sector, analysts said.
"You've seen how the other stocks have run: this has lagged," said an analyst who declined to be identified. "It's catching up."

Hudson's Bay was up by as much as 1.75 to a new 52-week high of 27.25, and were trading 1.60 higher at 27.10 on nearly 200,000 shares at midday. The shares rose from a recent low of 24 on February 10.
Analyst Bill Chisholm at Deacon Capital Corp added: "Merchandising stocks have been strong in the last 10 days ... this is a continuation."
Hudson's Bay shares are approaching heights of they have not reached since since mid-October 1995. Shares hit a low of 16 in mid-March of 1996.
The merchandising sector, which makes up 3.33 percent of the key 300 Composite Index, has steadily risen 6.5 percent from a low of 4808 points on February 10 to 5121 today.
